subhypothesis: At the fixed saved94 weights, SNP-conditioned upward-state and edge-message variation within persistent age-and-ordered-subtree groups may concentrate in a small shared32-channel subspace, making adaptive low-rank correction worth investigating.
data: Existing observed TRAIN000 first128 contiguous marginal trees, all1600 samples and681 source SNPs; diagnostic slice only, no simulation or production data changes.
procedure: One FP32 CPU call to saved-model prepare_tree_base_v1 and first full-depth cavity sweep on the exact packet. No second sweep/history/GRU, optimizer, predictions, truth or CUDA. Reconstruct original supplied level/child/rank order across all128 holds.
canonical_census: Compare strict source-ID census with primitive-input computational keys. Include exact raw site-MLP input bytes and original global256-site chunk segmentation, span, reference role/age, node-age/root/sample primitives, exact9 gate source bytes, parent degree and ordered children. Never merge solely on hidden numeric equality; preserve haplotype/readout/history routes.
groups: Same native observed node ID plus age/root/sample-ID/ordered-subtree signature; edge-message groups additionally retain incoming native parent, fixed edge geometry and degree. Groups with one occurrence carry no within-group evidence.
spectrum: Center within each group, then form a shared32x32 FP32 residual covariance. Report singular-energy fractions ranks1/2/4/8/16, both equal-occurrence and physical-span weighting; residual/total energy and pointwise p99/max reconstruction errors. This is a shared-channel low-rank diagnostic, not a per-group adaptive-rank or accuracy result.
interpretation: A steep spectrum can motivate a separately registered support-respecting interval or structural-plus-low-rank correction experiment. Poor concentration rejects a blind small-rank shortcut. Aggregate L2 energy alone cannot establish accuracy near rare ancestry boundaries. No superiority, novelty or whole-parent equivalence claim.
